\paragraph{Frozen theorem contract.}
Let $d\geq2$, let $B_d$ be the open cubical block with vertices
$\{0,1,2\}^d$, and put $m=2(d-1)$.  Let $G$ be a compact connected Lie group
with a bi-invariant Riemannian metric, let $p_t$ be the heat kernel of
$\tfrac12\Delta$ based at the identity, and choose
$z\in\mathrm Z(G)\setminus\{\mathbf1\}$.  For a full-degree link there is a
center-valued assignment of all other links that produces $m-1$ identity
staples and one $z^{-1}$ staple.  The conditional link law is proportional to
\[
  p_t(U)^{m-1}p_t(z^{-1}U)\,\mathrm dU.
\]
Writing $L=\operatorname{dist}(\mathbf1,z)$ and
$b_*=(m-1)L/m$, its normalized small-time rate is
\[
 (m-1)\operatorname{dist}(\mathbf1,U)^2
 +\operatorname{dist}(z,U)^2-\frac{m-1}{m}L^2.
\]
For every $0<\rho<b_*$, the conditional probability that the frustrated
plaquette lies within distance $\rho$ of the identity has logarithmic limit
$-m(b_*-\rho)^2$ at scale $2t$.  This remains exponentially small uniformly
on an open positive-Haar-measure neighborhood of the boundary assignment.
For the total-variation Dobrushin coefficients of the microscopic link
specification, the selected row sum is greater than one for sufficiently
small $t$.

The only limit is $t\downarrow0$ at fixed finite block and fixed metric.
There is no lattice-spacing, volume, continuum, or spectral limit in the
claim.
